records.name: Philly Frontrunners
records.summary: An LGBT+ running group for the LGBT+ community and allies in Philadelphia. It has met since 1983 and runs a Saturday morning route and a Monday evening route each week, often followed by a social.
records.what_you_do: Run or walk a 1, 3 or 5 mile route, then join the group for brunch or a social. Routes are shared on the group's Strava club.

schedule.text: Saturdays at 9:30 am from Lloyd Hall, and Mondays at 7 pm from William Way Community Center

locations.label: William Way Community Center, Spruce Street (Monday start)

cost.text: Dues are not stated on the group's site

first_step.how: Show up at a Saturday or Monday start, or join the group's mailing list from its website
first_step.basis: All abilities are welcome and walkers are welcome too, but the site names no beginner group

records.notes: The group's own site shows a 2018 copyright and events only from 2018 and 2019, so the newest recent evidence is the April 2025 Billy Penn guide. The site could not be reached at phillyfrontrunners.org or .com. Older writeups disagree about dues, so cost is left unknown.

records.name: Philly Runners
records.summary: An all-paces running club based in Center City, founded in 2002. It runs several times a week and says no one is turned away for pace or distance.
records.what_you_do: Join a Tuesday or Thursday evening run or a Saturday morning run, then get food or coffee together after. Members also volunteer at the Philadelphia race weekends.

schedule.text: Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:30 pm and Saturdays at 9 am (8 am from Memorial Day to Labor Day), all starting at the bottom of the Art Museum steps

locations.label: Bottom of the Art Museum steps, in front of the Visitors' Center

cost.text: Free: the site says there is no fee to join

first_step.how: Just show up at a run. An optional weekly email list is on the club's site.
first_step.basis: The site says everyone is welcome at every run regardless of pace or distance, and that no sign-up is needed

records.notes: The site lists a Mayor's Cup meetup dated August 8, 2026 and Philadelphia Marathon volunteering dated November 2026. The Thursday speed work time is shown on the site; the page's note about when that change took effect does not give a year, so it is not used as evidence.

records.name: Fishtown Beer Runners
records.summary: A weekly social run that has met every Thursday since 2007. Runners go at their own pace, then finish at a pub for a drink or two.
records.what_you_do: Run 3 to 5 miles at your own pace from one of three start points, then stay for a drink at the bar. Walkers and non-drinkers are welcome too.

schedule.text: Thursdays at 7 pm, starting from Palmer Park in Fishtown, from 7th and Bainbridge in Bella Vista, or from the City Hall courtyard

locations.label: Palmer Park, Frankford and Palmer streets (Fishtown start)

cost.text: No membership or dues. Runners pay for their own drinks.

first_step.how: Show up at one of the Thursday start points at 7 pm
first_step.basis: The site says all abilities are welcome and that no sign-up is needed

records.notes: The site lists upcoming runs on October 8 and October 15, 2026. It says the club is open to anyone over 21. The April 2025 Billy Penn guide lists the same Thursday start.

records.name: Issa Run Crew
records.summary: A Philadelphia running crew that meets for three regular runs each week: an easy evening run, a track workout, and a Saturday morning run with coffee and donuts. All paces are welcome.
records.what_you_do: Run with the crew at your own pace, then share coffee or donuts after the Saturday run.

schedule.text: Mondays with a 6 pm run start, Thursday track workouts at Temple Sports Complex, and Saturdays at 8 am from Lloyd Hall

cost.text: Cost is not stated on the site

first_step.how: Show up at a run, or email the crew at the address on its site
first_step.basis: The site says all paces are welcome and that you just have to show up

records.notes: The site's dated items are photo galleries from 2019. The April 2025 Billy Penn guide lists the same three weekly runs, which is the newest dated evidence.

records.name: Wynnefield Track Club
records.summary: A group of training partners in West Philadelphia who run together most mornings from Lloyd Hall. The club says its purpose is health and wellness in the community.
records.what_you_do: Join a morning run at Lloyd Hall, a track workout at St. Joseph's University, or a tempo run in the evening.

schedule.text: Most weekday mornings at 5:30 am from Lloyd Hall, track and tempo workouts on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and weekend early-morning runs

locations.label: St. Joseph's University, Sweeney Field (Tuesday track)

cost.text: Free, per the April 2025 Billy Penn guide. The club's site does not say.

first_step.how: Show up at Lloyd Hall, or email the club
first_step.basis: The site says all levels are welcome and to just show up, but its posts date from 2020

records.notes: The site's dated posts are from June 2020, and some blog posts are placeholders. The site gives Sunday at 6:30 am and the April 2025 guide gives 7 am, so the weekend time is left general. Confirm by email before going.

records.name: South Philly Striders
records.summary: A running club for South Philadelphia, Penn's Landing, Old City and Queen Village. It holds regular group runs, a yearly holiday lights run, and social meetups.
records.what_you_do: Join a weekly group run, or the yearly holiday lights run, which includes a food drive for local food banks.

schedule.text: Tuesday and Thursday runs at 6:15 am and Saturday runs at 8 am from Front and South streets, plus a Thursday 6:30 pm bridge run from 6th and Race streets

cost.text: Not stated on the club's site

first_step.how: Follow the club's message board or Facebook group to find the next run
first_step.basis: The site says all paces are welcome at its holiday run but gives no beginner information

records.notes: The newest dated item is a post dated November 24, 2025, for a December 11, 2025 holiday lights run. The weekly run times come from the April 2025 Billy Penn guide because the club's site does not list them.

records.name: Latinas In Motion
records.summary: A group that helps women get active, with a focus on Latina women. Members range from new exercisers to runners, according to the site's stories.
records.what_you_do: Join a group walk or run every other Saturday morning at Lorimer Park, and connect with the group on Facebook.

cost.text: Cost is not stated

records.name: West Philly Runners
records.summary: A running community in West Philadelphia that meets for a weekly group run and a speed workout.
records.what_you_do: Join the Wednesday group run, where you pick a 2, 4 or 6 mile route, or the Monday speed workout.

first_step.how: Use the Facebook group link on the club's site to see the next run

records.notes: The site's only event is an October 14 run with no year shown, so the status rests on the April 2025 Billy Penn guide. The times and places come from that guide.

records.name: Queer Run
records.summary: A free run club for LGBTQIA+ runners and allies in Philadelphia. It is a nonprofit and meets for short runs several times a week.
records.what_you_do: Meet at a posted spot for a 3 or 4 mile run at any pace. You do not need to sign up, just show up at the spot.

schedule.text: Mondays at 7 pm (3 miles, from the center of Rittenhouse Square), Wednesdays at 6 pm (3 miles, from Manayunk), and Thursdays at 6 am (4 miles, from the southwest corner of Love Park)

cost.text: Free

first_step.how: Show up at the posted meeting spot at run time, or email the group

records.name: Men's Night Run Club

records.what_you_do: Register for a weekly night run on Eventbrite, then run with the group and take part in its wellness and community events.

schedule.text: Thursdays at 7:30 pm, per the April 2025 Billy Penn guide. The group's own site points to Eventbrite for dates.

first_step.basis: The sign-up path is public and open to men 18 and up, but the site does not describe what a first run is like

records.name: Mural Miles

first_step.how: Follow the group on Instagram for the next run's details

records.name: Girls on the Run Philadelphia
records.summary: A program that uses running and group talks to help girls build confidence and healthy habits. Teams meet during the season, and adults can volunteer as coaches.
records.what_you_do: Girls join a team for a season of practices that ends with a 5K. Volunteers help coach and run each team.

schedule.text: Team practices run during the season. Days and times are set for each team and are not shown on the site.

locations.label: Program office, 40 W Evergreen Ave, Suite 104

cost.text: Fees are not stated. The site says no girl is turned away because of money.

records.name: Bicycle Coalition Youth Cycling
records.summary: A youth cycling program in Philadelphia, run by the Bicycle Coalition, that teaches cycling along with teamwork, goal setting and school success. It was formerly called Cadence Youth Cycling.

locations.label: Bicycle Coalition office, 1500 Walnut St (not a practice site)

cost.text: Fees are not stated. The site asks for donations to support the program.

first_step.how: The site gives no sign-up steps. Call the Bicycle Coalition office at 215-242-9253 to ask about teams.
first_step.basis: The page does not explain how families join, so the way in is unclear

notes:
Searches: all 3 used, on running and cycling club discovery. Fetches: 57, including failed and redirected ones. Budget was not exhausted before the list was done, but the fetch cap was reached near the end, so the leads below are unchecked.

Search gaps: no search was run for walking groups for older adults, so none are recorded and this part of the slice is not done. Philadelphia Gearing Up was not found: gearingup.org redirects to an unrelated motorcycle training program in Canada, so it is not used.

RRCA: the RRCA directory's Pennsylvania entries show suburban clubs only (for example Delco, Bryn Mawr, Ambler, Bucks County, Chester County). None are in the city, so none are recorded.

Domains that did not resolve: phillyfrontrunners.org and .com (the real site is phillyfr.org), cadenceyouthcycling.org, bicycleclubofphiladelphia.org, pcaphila.org, nbwphilly.org. bicycleclub.org returned no content. The Neighborhood Bike Works shop address printed as 3939 Lancaster Ave on its site, with a different mailing number, so 3939 is used. novemberproject.com is a parked domain.

Dropped after fetch, with reasons: Wharton Roadrunners and Triathletes (a student club; eligibility and weekly times not shown). ACCT Philly Runners (the shelter site has no runner volunteer program). Women in Ultrarunning (no Philadelphia chapter on the site). Guy's Racing (certificate error).

Hidden as out of scope: Furthur Training and Racing and Philly Surge Running, both paid coaching businesses.

Sources of dating: the Billy Penn running guide (April 28, 2025) is the main list and the newest dated evidence for many groups. Its page shows an update date of August 7, 2026, but the entries are dated April 2025, so entries are recorded as 2025-04. Most leads are Instagram or Facebook only and were not fetched.

Record count: 22 publish and 2 hide, which is under the 25 target because the fetch cap was reached and two list entries had no usable site. Many statuses rest on the April 2025 guide because the group sites carry no current dates.
